objective: Publish the release tags only after the manifest verification, attestation and promotion check have all passed, so a failed release leaves no tagged artifact behind.
decision_supported: Can the release tags be published last, after the evidence that authorizes them, while still attesting a real registry digest rather than a local image id?
acceptance: No release tag is pushed before the manifest is written, verified, attested and checked for promotion.
The image is still attested against a real registry digest, so a staging push happens first under a tag no consumer resolves as a release.
Every release tag is moved onto that staged digest rather than onto a local image id.
A run that publishes zero tags fails instead of passing quietly.
The attestation step targets the staged digest, not a publish-step output that no longer exists.
A test asserts the step order and fails when a publish step is moved earlier.
evidence: Before the change the workflow pushed the release tags at the Publish tested image step, wrote the manifest 28 lines later and verified promotion after that.
A failure in any of the later steps therefore left the pushed tag in GHCR with no successful provenance or attestation evidence for it.
Moving the publish block back before the manifest step makes the new ordering test fail; restoring it passes 11.
stop_conditions: The attestation action cannot target a digest that is not a release tag; it can, because it takes subject-name and subject-digest separately.
The registry rejects a push that moves an existing tag; tags are immutable in this repository only if configured so, and moving one is the intended behaviour on a re-run.
risks_and_fallbacks: A failed release now leaves a staging-<sha> tag in the registry instead of a release tag; that is visible in the registry but does not resolve as a version.
Pulling by digest before retagging costs one extra image pull per release tag, which is small next to the build.
